summary.headline: Vaibhav Global Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.7% to INR917 crore and EBITDA rose 37% to INR102 crore, but constant-currency revenue was broadly flat.
summary.overview:
Reported revenue grew 12.7% YoY to INR917 crore, EBITDA rose 37% to INR102 crore (margin 11% vs 9.2%), and PAT rose 50% to INR56 crore. Management said reported growth was helped by favourable FX and a U.S. tariff refund of about INR38 crore, of which INR25 crore sits in other operating revenue and flows fully to gross profit and EBITDA. Excluding the refund, B2C growth in USD was largely flat, with the U.S. up 4% and U.K. flat in local currency and Germany up 6%. FY27 guidance of 9-11% revenue growth and 50-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion was reiterated.</overview>

segments.name: U.S.
segments.commentary: Local-currency growth of 4% with U.S. revenue around INR530 crore; vertically integrated model helped margin expansion despite tariffs. Average ticket size fell from $50 to $46 while volume traction rose on lower price points.

segments.name: U.K.
segments.commentary: Flat overall; core TJC subdued but Ideal World grew at healthy double digits and Rachel Galley showed encouraging momentum.

segments.name: Germany
segments.commentary: Grew 6% in local currency with improving margins; EBITDA marginally above breakeven in Q1. Management expects positive contribution to group profit from FY27.

segments.name: Digital (B2C)
segments.commentary: 45% of B2C revenue; target to cross 50% during FY27. Digital volume flat at about 1.13 million orders while USD ticket size rose from $33.8 to $37.

segments.name: Television
segments.commentary: Revenue INR484 crore, up 9%; TV volume rose from 1.34 million to 1.37 million. TV networks reached about 127 million households.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 9-11% reiterated.
FY27 EBITDA margin expansion of 50-100 bps over FY26 reiterated.
Mid- to long-term growth ambition of 12-15%; FY30 revenue ambition of INR5,000-5,500 crore, with currency assumed to depreciate about 3% a year.
Management said margin will keep improving but declined to give a specific FY30 margin number.
Digital customer payback target cut from about 9-10 months to 3 months; ROAS for pure digital acquisition currently about 2, targeting 3+.
Germany expected to contribute positively to group profit from FY27.
capex_capacity: No capex figures disclosed in the call.
Migration of all key e-commerce platforms from Salesforce to Shopify Enterprise completed in Q1; management said initial hiccups over the past couple of months were still being worked through.
AI tools deployed across product scheduling, content generation, personalised marketing and demand forecasting.
Lab-grown diamonds about 13% of retail revenue; management sees 14-16% over coming years.
Buyback withheld until a $50-100 million cash cushion is built for acquisitions or other opportunities.
demand_pricing: Constant-currency revenue broadly flat, with Middle East conflict disruption early in the quarter and cautious consumers in key markets.
U.S. consumers prioritising essentials as fuel costs rose; management said lower price points are gaining traction.
Lab-grown diamond ASP about $250, which management says is supporting higher lifetime value customers.
Unique customers 6.77 lakh (moderated), retention 38%, trailing 12-month pieces per customer 23.
Management says marketplace take rate is about 0% because less than 0.5% of sales come through marketplaces.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY30 INR5,000-5,500 crore revenue target realistic, and what margin is implied?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target was set for a volatile macro and that margins will keep improving, driven by gross margin gains and digital mix. It declined to give a specific FY30 EBITDA margin number.

qa_highlights.question: Why no buyback, and why not a new India or new-brand initiative given free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: The company wants a $50-100 million cushion for opportunities before any buyback. India is seen as a later option, after digital scales and Germany becomes PAT positive.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 growth is from FX and pricing versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was mainly currency and tariff refund; ex-refund USD growth was largely flat. Volume rose on lower price points, while U.S. average ticket size fell from $50 to $46.

qa_highlights.question: How much was the tariff refund and where does it sit in the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR38 crore received: INR25 crore in other operating revenue (flows to gross profit and EBITDA) and INR13 crore kept in inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Digital ad spend and ROAS hurdle?
qa_highlights.answer: Spend continues while it earns double-digit margin over spend; ROAS on new customer acquisition is about 2, targeted at over 3.

qa_highlights.question: Why are digital volumes flat despite 21% digital revenue growth and 3.5 lakh new users?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital growth came mostly from currency (about 11 points) and higher ticket size (about 10 points) as the mix shifts to lab-grown; volume was flat at 1.13 million.

risks_watch: Constant-currency growth is flat; reported growth depends on FX and the one-time INR25 crore tariff refund, which flatters Q1 gross margin and EBITDA.
Customer count moderated and retention is 38%; management says digital retention and repeat will decline as acquisition scales.
Digital volumes flat YoY; growth relies on ticket size and lab-grown mix against competition.
Shopify migration hiccups may still be affecting digital sales.
FY30 target needs about 10% CAGR while the rupee is assumed to depreciate 3% a year; a flat currency would make this harder.
Disclosure: analysts asked for constant-currency growth by country and a clearer refund breakdown. Management said it would consider adding these to the presentation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on digital, margins and the balance sheet, but defensive on the flat constant-currency growth and the non-recurring refund. Management gave few numbers on the FY30 margin path and deflected buyback and India questions, citing macro volatility.
key_quotes: And I'm pleased to confirm that the business is now on track to contribute positively to group profitability from FY '27, consistent with the trajectory we had guided to.
The ROAS is roughly around right now currently at 2. And we are expecting to expand to over 3 in coming years.
